pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Harvesters — reapers sit down to their meal in the stubble under a great pear tree, one tipping a brown jug up to drink and others spooning from wooden bowls and cutting bread on a white cloth, a man stretched out flat asleep with his arms thrown back against the trunk, the standing wheat still uncut in a deep gold block at the left and the cut sheaves stacked away behind them toward the village tower, one sabbath jesus was passing through the grainfields, and his disciples began to pick the heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat them, but some of the pharisees asked, why are you doing what is unlawful on the sabbath
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_harvesters

pictures.scene: Steen, Prayer Before the Meal — a mother in a white cap sits by the open window with her baby on her lap and her eyes closed, the father across from her holding his hat against his chest with his head bowed over his folded hands, a round brown loaf and a block of cheese set out on the white cloth between them with a dish of meat on the upturned barrel in front, a written board and a hanging wreath on the bare wall above, jesus replied, have you not read what david did when he and his companions were hungry, he entered the house of god, took the consecrated bread and gave it to his companions, and ate what is lawful only for the priests to eat
pictures.name: pd_steen_prayer_before_the_meal

pictures.scene: Brandon, Scene in a Synagogue — a man in a broad hat and a pale gold prayer shawl carries the dressed Torah scroll down from the ark with its silver crowns above his shoulder, a boy in a long robe holding up a lit taper to meet him at the foot of the steps and another worshipper bowing low at the right with his hands raised, the congregation crowded along the carved rail in the shadow behind, then jesus declared, the son of man is lord of the sabbath, on another sabbath jesus entered the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there whose right hand was withered
pictures.name: pd_brandon_scene_in_a_synagogue

pictures.scene: Tidemand, The Haugians — a young man in a white homespun jacket and a red waistcoat stands up on a low stool in the middle of the room holding a small open book in both hands, the farm people drawn in a close ring around him on chairs and on the floor, one old man with his arms folded, another leaning his chin on both fists, a woman bowed over with her face hidden in her hands, a shaft of light coming down through the dark loft above them, looking for a reason to accuse jesus, the scribes and pharisees were watching him closely to see if he would heal on the sabbath, but jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, get up and stand among us, so he got up and stood there
pictures.name: pd_tidemand_haugianerne

pictures.scene: Poussin, Peter and John Healing the Lame Man — a bearded apostle in a heavy gold cloak sits on the temple step pointing upward with one hand while he stretches the other down open to the crippled man sprawled at his feet, his fair-haired companion in rose and green leaning in beside him with both hands held out over the man, onlookers crowding close from either side under the great dark column, the pale city wall and the blue cloud-strewn sky standing over the whole step, then jesus said to them, i ask you, which is lawful on the sabbath, to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it, and after looking around at all of them, he said to the man, stretch out your hand, he did so, and it was restored
pictures.name: pd_poussin_healing_lame_man

pictures.scene: Van Gogh, The Starry Night — the whole night sky rolls over in one great swirl of blue and white brushstrokes with eleven burning stars and a crescent moon set in haloes of yellow light around it, a dark cypress climbing like a flame up the left side of the picture from bottom to top, the blue hills running along below the sky and the little town asleep under them with its church spire standing up into the stars, but the scribes and pharisees were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what they might do to jesus, in those days jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and he spent the night in prayer to god
pictures.name: pd_van_gogh_the_starry_night

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Saint Peter Preaching — a white-bearded apostle in a blue tunic and a great orange cloak stands barefoot on the stone with one hand raised in blessing and the other holding his mantle, speaking out over the people pressed in close around him, two women kneeling at his feet with their heads covered and an old man in red bowing beside them, a crowd of listeners in caps and hoods ranked up behind on the right with their faces all turned toward him, the green wooded hillside rising behind the whole gathering, when daylight came, he called his disciples to him and chose twelve of them, whom he also designated as apostles, simon, whom he named peter, and his brother andrew, james and john, philip and bartholomew
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_saint_peter_preaching

pictures.scene: Juanes, The Last Supper — Christ sits at the middle of the long white table holding up the round loaf in one raised hand with the other laid on His breast and the gold chalice standing in front of Him, grey-bearded Peter pressing a hand to his heart at His right and young John in green turning to Him open-mouthed at His left, both their names lettered in the gold haloes above their heads, more disciples reaching in from the edge, the bread and the dishes and the knives laid down the cloth and the bare feet of the apostles showing under the table on the tiled floor, the arched window behind opening on a green evening country, matthew and thomas, james son of alphaeus and simon called the zealot, judas son of james, and judas iscariot, who became a traitor
pictures.name: pd_juanes_last_supper

pictures.scene: Repin, Religious Procession in Kursk Province — a great crowd comes across the open dusty plain behind the gold embroidered banners and the jewelled icon carried high at the head of it, a hunched lame boy in a long grey coat pushing out ahead of them all in the foreground with his crutch under one arm and his stick swung out in front of him, an overseer stepping in to hold him back, a priest in a heavy gold vestment walking at the right and a woman in a pale flounced dress carrying a small icon in the middle of the throng, the mounted guard at the left edge and the bare hills and the wide pale sky standing over the whole march, then jesus came down with them and stood on a level place, a large crowd of his disciples was there, along with a great number of people from all over judea, jerusalem, and the sea coast of tyre and sidon, they had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases, and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed
pictures.name: pd_repin_religious_procession_in_kursk_province

pictures.scene: Master of Alkmaar, Feeding the Hungry — a woman in a white headdress and a long white apron carries a basket heaped with round loaves out of her doorway into the street, a young man in a black cap at her shoulder reaching into it to hand the bread on, Christ standing quietly among the poor behind them, a mother in a green gown passing a loaf across to an old man in a red cloak while the child at her side stretches both arms up for it, a crippled beggar pushing himself along the cobbles on his wooden hand blocks at the bottom of the picture and a dog sitting watching him, the tall brick houses and stepped gables of the town rising away behind, the entire crowd was trying to touch him, because power was coming from him and healing them all, looking up at his disciples, jesus said, blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of god
pictures.name: pd_alkmaar_barmhartigheid

pictures.scene: Van Gogh, Sorrowing Old Man — a white-haired old man in a worn blue labourer's suit sits doubled over on a plain rush-seated chair with both fists pressed hard against his face and his elbows driven into his knees, his heavy clouted boots planted apart on the bare board floor, the red chair and the yellow boards and the papered wall worked over in short strokes all around him and no one else in the room, blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled, blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh, blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the son of man
pictures.name: pd_van_gogh_sorrowing_old_man

pictures.scene: Zorn, Midsummer Dance — village people are dancing on the grass outside the grey log barn in the pale light of a midsummer night, a girl in a white embroidered blouse and a long black skirt swung round in the arms of a young man in a black hat and red braces, more couples whirling past behind them with their white sleeves catching the light, others standing along the barn wall in dark coats and hats to watch, the red farmhouse with its lit windows and the tall garlanded maypole standing up against the bright sky, rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven, for their fathers treated the prophets in the same way, but woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort
pictures.name: pd_zorn_midsommardans

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Parable of the Rich Fool — an old man in a fur-edged black cap and a gold-braided coat leans in close over the one candle burning on his table in the dark, holding a coin up to the flame with his spectacles slipped down his nose and his hand cupped round the light to see it by, the money bags and the little weighing scales and the heaped bundles of papers crowding the table beside him, a stack of gold counted out on the cloth by the candlestick and the ledgers piled away into the shadow behind him, woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger, woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep, woe to you when all men speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_parable_of_the_rich_fool

pictures.scene: Gottlieb, Jews Praying in the Synagogue on Yom Kippur — a bearded man in a tall fur hat and a striped prayer shawl carries the covered scroll in both arms through the crowded hall with his eyes lowered, a young man at his shoulder pressing a hand against his forehead inside his shawl, another bowed right down onto the reading desk with his face in the open book, a white-bearded elder praying behind them, the women leaning over the rail of the gallery above in embroidered head cloths, a small boy standing at the front looking straight out, the great stone pillar and the dim arches of the vault going up over all of them, but to those of you who will listen, i say, love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you
pictures.name: pd_gottlieb_jews_praying_on_yom_kippur

pictures.scene: Chardin, The Return from the Market — a servant woman in a white cap and a long blue apron over full white sleeves stands just inside the kitchen with her marketing still in her hands, a loaf tied up in a white cloth hanging from one hand and a striped bag slung at her side, two great round loaves and a stoneware jug set down on the walnut sideboard beside her with a pewter dish leaning up behind them, a dark wine bottle standing on the stone floor in the corner, her head turned away over her shoulder to answer someone in the next room, if someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also, and if someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic as well, give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back
pictures.name: pd_chardin_la_pourvoyeuse

pictures.scene: De Wet, Christ Blessing the Children — Christ sits on the stone step in a pale robe with a dull red cloak across His knees and a faint ring of light round His bowed head, one hand laid on His breast as He leans down to the children brought in to Him, a mother in a blue gown kneeling at the left with her baby held up on her arm, a little girl in a yellow dress kneeling right in front of Him with her hands pressed together, a boy in a red cap sitting on the paving with his back turned, a small child being lifted toward Him from the right, the bearded men standing watching from the dark doorway behind, do to others as you would have them do to you, if you love those who love you, what credit is that to you, even sinners love those who love them
pictures.name: pd_dewet_christus_zegent_kinderen

pictures.scene: Reymerswaele, A Moneychanger and His Wife — a moneychanger in a great ruffled red cap and a fur-lined gown bends over his table with his fingers on the beam of the little hand balance, weighing one coin against the weight, his wife leaning in at his side in a white linen headdress and a rose gown with her eyes down on the scales, a canvas money bag slumped open on the table between them, the board in front of them spread with loose silver and stacked columns of gold and a folded paper, the ledger and the guttered candle standing on the shelf behind, if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you, even sinners do the same, and if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you, even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full
pictures.name: pd_van_reymerswaele_a_moneychanger_and_his_wife

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Jacob Blessing the Sons of Joseph — the dying old man raises himself on the deep red coverlet of his bed in a white shirt and a gold cap and lays his open hand down across the head of the fair-haired younger boy, Joseph in a great pale turban leaning over him from behind with one hand supporting his father's arm and the other lifted as if to move the blessing hand across, the dark-haired elder brother watching with his chin just over the edge of the bed, their mother standing at the right in a dark gown and a jewelled headdress with her hands quietly down, but love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return, then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the most high, for he is kind to the ungrateful and wicked, be merciful, just as your father is merciful
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_jacob_blessing_the_sons_of_joseph

pictures.scene: Millet, The Sower — a sower in a broad hat and a short brown jacket comes striding down the ploughed slope at dusk with the seed bag gathered up against his hip in one arm and the other hand swung wide out of it, scattering the grain as he walks, his blue trousers and his bound straw leggings dark against the turned earth under his feet, the long hillside rising away behind him to a thin band of evening sky with the last light still on a far ridge, do not judge, and you will not be judged, do not condemn, and you will not be condemned, forgive, and you will be forgiven, give, and it will be given to you, a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over will be poured into your lap, for with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_sower

pictures.scene: Teniers, The Blind Leading the Blind — a blind man in a long tan coat gropes his way down the lane with his staff held up in one fist and a pewter can swung out in the other, his face turned blindly away from the path in front of him, the man behind him already gone over backwards onto the bank at the right with his legs thrown up and his hand still caught in the leader's coat, a boy in a white shirt carrying a black case walking close at his elbow and a smaller child pressed against his side, the heavy brown trees and the broken sky standing over the whole lane, jesus also told them a parable, can a blind man lead a blind man, will they not both fall into a pit, a disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher
pictures.name: pd_teniers_the_blind_leading_the_blind

pictures.scene: Millais, Christ in the House of His Parents — a red-haired boy in a long pale smock stands barefoot at the carpenter's bench holding up His cut palm, His mother down on one knee in a deep blue gown and a white head cloth with her face lifted to His, the carpenter leaning right across the bench from the other side to take the hand and look into the wound, an old woman in an orange shawl watching from the far end with the pincers still in her fingers, the fresh planks and the half-made door laid over the trestles, the saw and the set square hanging on the boarded wall and the curled wood shavings scattered over the floor, why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye, how can you say, brother, let me take the speck out of your eye, while you yourself fail to see the beam in your own eye
pictures.name: pd_millais_carpenter

pictures.scene: Pissarro, Orchard in Bloom at Louveciennes — an old fruit tree stands in the middle of the picture in full white blossom with its branches spread right across the frame and the light coming through them, a second tree leaning in from the right with its low bough reaching out over the ground, the brown turned earth of the orchard worked over in broad strokes below and a line of smaller trees standing back in the haze behind, a woman in a blue skirt and a white cap bent down low over her work beside the cut logs at the left, the blue spring sky and its heaped white clouds showing along the top, you hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother's eye, no good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit
pictures.name: pd_pissarro_orchard_in_bloom_louveciennes

pictures.scene: Melendez, Still Life with Figs and Bread — a white earthenware dish heaped with ripe figs stands on the bare kitchen table, the green ones and the split purple ones piled over each other with their stalks still on and the grain of their skins painted out one by one, torn round loaves of coarse country bread stacked up behind the dish with the crumb showing where they are broken open, a brass-handled knife laid down on the boards in front, a dark green wine bottle with its cork in standing at the back beside a wooden water tub and a coopered pail bound with iron, the plain brown wall going up behind them all, for each tree is known by its own fruit, indeed, figs are not gathered from thornbushes, nor grapes from brambles, the good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart, for out of the overflow of the heart, the mouth speaks
pictures.name: pd_melendez_figs_and_bread

pictures.scene: Hofmann, Christ and the Rich Young Ruler — Christ stands against the pale stone wall in a dull red robe with a dark blue-green cloak hung over His shoulder, His face turned calmly toward the young man and His hand reaching out open and low in front of Him, the young man standing close at His side in a jewelled turban and a heavy cream mantle over a green silk sleeve and an embroidered sash, his eyes dropped and his face set and unhappy, both his hands held down and clasped away from the hand that is offered to him, the plain blocks of the wall going up behind the two of them, why do you call me lord, lord, but not do what i say, i will show you what he is like who comes to me and hears my words and acts on them
pictures.name: pd_hofmann_christ_and_the_rich_young_ruler

pictures.scene: Ruisdael, Waterfall in a Rocky Landscape — a swollen torrent comes down the whole bottom half of the picture in white broken water, driving round the great red-brown boulders that stand up out of it and pouring away over the shelves of rock in the foreground, a timber bridge thrown across the stream above the fall with two small travellers crossing it, a bare rock bluff standing over the water in the middle with a steep-roofed house and its chimney set up on the height behind, dark firs and wind-torn trees crowding the banks on both sides, the piled storm clouds breaking open to a strip of blue over the hills beyond, he is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock, when the flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it was well built, but the one who hears my words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation, the torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell, and great was its destruction
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_waterfall_in_a_rocky_landscape

lines.text: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat them.
But some of the Pharisees asked, Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?
Jesus replied, Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
He entered the house of God, took the consecrated bread and gave it to his companions, and ate what is lawful only for the priests to eat.
Then Jesus declared, The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.
On another Sabbath Jesus entered the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there whose right hand was withered.
Looking for a reason to accuse Jesus, the scribes and Pharisees were watching Him closely to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.
But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, Get up and stand among us. So he got up and stood there.
Then Jesus said to them, I ask you, which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?
And after looking around at all of them, He said to the man, Stretch out your hand. He did so, and it was restored.
But the scribes and Pharisees were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus.
In those days Jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and He spent the night in prayer to God.
When daylight came, He called His disciples to Him and chose twelve of them, whom He also designated as apostles:
Simon, whom He named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew;
Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus and Simon called the Zealot;
Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.

Then Jesus came down with them and stood on a level place. A large crowd of His disciples was there, along with a great number of people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon.
They had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases, and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.
The entire crowd was trying to touch Him, because power was coming from Him and healing them all.
Looking up at His disciples, Jesus said: Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.
Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven. For their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.
But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort.
Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.
But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also. And if someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic as well.
Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.
Do to others as you would have them do to you.
If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.
If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.
And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.

But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.
Jesus also told them a parable: Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?
A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.
Why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?
How can you say, Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye, while you yourself fail to see the beam in your own eye?
You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother's eye.
No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.
For each tree is known by its own fruit. Indeed, figs are not gathered from thornbushes, nor grapes from brambles.

The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart. For out of the overflow of the heart, the mouth speaks.
Why do you call Me Lord, Lord, but not do what I say?
I will show you what he is like who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them:

He is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock. When the flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it was well built.

But the one who hears My words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation. The torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell, and great was its destruction!
